---
title: "dplyr recap: select() and filter() (solutions)"
format: html
---

Teacher version. Chunks run, so `data/flights.csv` must exist.

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(here, tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
flights <- read_csv(here("data", "flights.csv"))
```

## Your turn 1: select a range

```{r}
#| label: turn-1a
flights |>
  select(dep_time:arr_delay)
```

Answer: 6 columns (`dep_time`, `sched_dep_time`, `dep_delay`, `arr_time`, `sched_arr_time`, `arr_delay`).

```{r}
#| label: turn-1b
flights |>
  select(!dep_time:arr_delay)
```

Answer: 13 columns, the 19 of `flights` minus 6.

## Your turn 2: select by pattern

```{r}
#| label: turn-2a
flights |>
  select(ends_with("time"))
```

Answer: 5 columns (`dep_time`, `sched_dep_time`, `arr_time`, `sched_arr_time`, `air_time`). `time_hour` ends in `hour`, so it stays out.

```{r}
#| label: turn-2b
flights |>
  select(starts_with("sched"))
```

Answer: 2 columns (`sched_dep_time`, `sched_arr_time`).

## Your turn 3: AND and OR

```{r}
#| label: turn-3a
flights |>
  filter(month == 12 & day == 25)
```

```{r}
#| label: turn-3b
flights |>
  filter(month == 6 | month == 7)
```

```{r}
#| label: turn-3c
flights |>
  filter(month %in% c(6, 7))
```

Answer: both versions return the same number of rows. Students check it by adding `count()` to each chunk.

## Your turn 4: NOT

```{r}
#| label: turn-4a
flights |>
  filter(origin != "JFK") |>
  count(origin)
```

Answer: 2 airports remain (EWR and LGA).

```{r}
#| label: turn-4b
flights |>
  filter(!(origin %in% c("JFK", "LGA"))) |>
  count(origin)
```

Answer: EWR is the only airport left.

## Notes for the teacher

- Slide checks: `month == 1 & month == 2` returns 0 rows. `month == 1 | month == 2` and `month %in% c(1, 2)` return the same rows. `month == 1 | 2` returns all 12 months. `month != 1 & month != 2` and `!(month %in% c(1, 2))` return the same rows.
- `filter(dep_delay == NA)` returns 0 rows. `filter(is.na(dep_delay))` returns the flights with a missing departure delay. This needs the full `flights` table, which has missing values.
- Spare slide if a student asks: `filter(month != 1 | month != 2)` returns every row, because every month differs from 1 or from 2. The fix is `&`.
